video_title: YouTube title: BRIAN WINDHORST ON THE 76ERS ADDING JAYLEN BROWN & LEBRON JAMES

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on James Harden leaving the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: He now has to be very careful when he talks to me. Now it's a source relationship.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: I would think James Harden picks up and leaves and becomes an executive in the NBA and leaves your Hoop Collective podcast, which is so great. Are you angry at him? Will you ever talk to him again?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: He now has to be very careful when he talks to me. Now it's a source relationship, but I think I got to start buying his meals. That's what's so annoying.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' decision to join the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: We didn't know that him wanting to win the championship this year was the number one priority.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: You have known LeBron James since he was a teenager in high school. Were you surprised at his choice of the 76ers?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I was, of course. I didn't have the full information. We didn't know that him wanting to win the championship this year was the number one priority. It's easy to say that of course you want to win the championship every year, but that's what we didn't really know. He left the Lakers and he said he wanted happiness, and that can mean different things to different people.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Joel Embiid's health and the 76ers' championship potential
quotes.excerpt: Without Joel Embiid, are they a championship level team?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: To me, I look at that squad, Brian, and I go, well, Joel Embiid has to be healthy. He can't go into this thinking that Joel Embiid is going to be healthy. He's never healthy. So without Joel Embiid, are they a championship level team?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: It's a great question and I of course agree. He can't assume that. He's barely played the last three years.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The 76ers' defensive struggles against the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: The last time we saw the 76ers, the New York Knicks were ripping them on both sides.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: What about the 76ers' defense?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The last time we saw the 76ers, the New York Knicks were ripping them on both sides of the court, and particularly defensively. They attacked Joel Embiid. They used Jaylen Brown as an attacker. That was their strategy. They found the pigeon, right? That was their strategy. They found the pigeon and went to work. Mike Brown talking about the way they put James Harden in knots, if you remember, and that's what they did to Joel Embiid. Of the 16 teams that made the playoffs, the 76ers ranked 14th in defense in terms of their defensive rating.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of integrating Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, and LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: Is there enough basketball for Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey? Well, now we add LeBron James.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: Before LeBron James signed on with them, I was talking to someone I know, a very well-known person in the NBA, and he said the thing that he feared the most about them getting Jaylen Brown was, is there enough basketball for Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey? Well, now we add LeBron James into the equation, who always averages 20 points. Is there enough basketball for the three of them?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: That's a great question because to me, the challenge for the 76ers is not LeBron James. The challenge for the 76ers is Jaylen Brown. Jaylen Brown didn't sign up for this. Jaylen didn't wake up and say, I want to be a 76er. It was put on him. I'm sure he wanted LeBron to play for the team, but this is not something that Jaylen was looking for at this time in his career. He's in his prime. He's trying to win MVPs. He's trying to elevate his team to the highest level. He's trying to get another max contract.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's performance and advanced metrics
quotes.excerpt: All I keep reading about is how Jaylen Brown is just a bad player regarding the numbers.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: I watch the games as a fan with some inside knowledge, and all I keep reading about is how Jaylen Brown is just a bad player when it comes to the numbers, the inside-under-the-hood numbers. Why am I not seeing that he's a bad player, but why are the numbers saying that he's not the player I think I'm seeing?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: There's a little bit more nuance to it than that. It's not that he's a bad player and it's not that his numbers are terrible. It's that for 57 million, the numbers don't compute.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of the Knicks extending Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.excerpt: One of the most important things to still happen in this summer is how much the Knicks pay.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: What is the most important thing to happen this summer?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: In the modern NBA, what you pay your top players is vital, and that's why, arguably, one of the most important things to still happen in this summer is how much the Knicks pay Karl-Anthony Towns on an extension. Because the hardest thing to do in the NBA is to win a championship. The second hardest thing to do in the NBA is to keep a championship window open. It crushed the Bucks. It crushed the Celtics. The Denver Nuggets are holding on by the skin of their teeth. The Thunder are chopping off fingers. The Knicks made this decision trying to hold their championship window open.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' potential move to the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I always thought that if the Knicks had not won this year, he would be a Knick.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: I always thought that if the Knicks had not won this year, he would be a Knick. Rich Paul kind of said that that would have been the case. Do you think the Knicks had a chance to bring him aboard even though they won the championship?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Yeah. How many hours of your life have you spent over the last 15 years devoted to talking about LeBron as a Knick? He's going to live, I think, part-time in New York in this season. He's ready at this point in his life to live in New York. Rich discussed that over 20 teams called him as soon as they heard LeBron was going to be on the market. I'm sure 18 had no chance. The Knicks didn't call. He called Leon. They had a cordial conversation and it ended. He wanted to play in New York.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green's comments on Jalen Brunson's contract
quotes.excerpt: I was interested in what Draymond Green said about Brunson taking 100 million dollars less.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: I was interested in what Draymond Green said about Brunson taking 100 million dollars less in his last contract. He said it was foolish because the star player should never take less. He said Steph has never taken less, I have to, Josh Hart should have to, the other guys should have to, not Brunson. He should have never done that. Do you see where Draymond Green is coming from?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Yeah, it's a great question. In a vacuum, yes, in a vacuum, you definitely should take every dollar because frankly, star players are underpaid. If Jalen Brunson was making the full max, he's underpaid. What's Jalen's value to the Knicks organization? It's in the hundreds of millions of dollars. And the fact that he'd be capped at 50 whatever million, that's already unfair as part of their labor deal.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's potential contract extension with the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: Steph can sign a contract extension this summer. Two years and about 140 million.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Kay
text_blocks.text: What about Steph?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: This is going to be on Steph's plate this summer. Steph can sign a contract extension this summer. Two years and about 140 million. He's earned every penny and if that's what he wants, the Warriors will give it to him in less than a second. But it might make sense, if Steph wants another championship, it might make sense to wait and clear that cap space next summer and see what happens and see if he can share his money and move it around to get another piece.
